result.title: The next tech shift is already here
result.description:
We've spent decades making new technologies bigger. But the next wave of #tech may be heading in the opposite direction. 

The World Economic Forum’s new Top 10 Emerging Technologies Report reveals a surprising pattern emerging across this year's breakthrough innovations:

#Energy systems powered by parked cars and buildings
#Medicines tailored to a single person
#Innovations that are becoming more local, distributed and personal

Hear from Kimmy Bettinger, who leads the report, as she unpacks the trends behind this year's most important emerging technologies. You can find about more about them in the report:  https://www.weforum.org/publications/top-10-emerging-technologies-of-2026

result.title: Summer Davos 2026 Highlights
result.description:
How do we turn today's technological breakthroughs into tomorrow's growth, jobs and opportunity?

That was the question at the heart of the 17th Annual Meeting of the New Champions known as #SummerDavos, where 1,500 leaders from business, government and academia gathered in Dalian, China.

This film captures the conversations, ideas and energy of the meeting, featuring insights from World Economic Forum Managing Directors on shared challenges - from AI to advanced manufacturing, clean energy to the investments needed to accelerate innovation at scale.

result.title: The Hormuz shock, AI and China: the state of global energy, with Jason Bordoff
result.description:
Is 2026 the year it all changed for energy?

The Strait of Hormuz closure was "the largest oil supply disruption in history" but has not (yet) brought the global economy to its knees. But are we now living in a post-Hormuz world where countries and companies are seeking to diversify energy supply and ramp up renewables?

Jason Bordoff of the Center on Global Energy Policy and the Columbia Energy Exchange podcast returns to Radio Davos, at the Forum's 'Summer Davos' in China, for an update on the global energy situation.
Co-hosted by Roberto Booca, head of the Forum's Centre for Energy and Materials.

result.title: It can take hours to fix ‘workslop’. Here's how to get rid of it
result.description:
Have you ever received poor-quality AI-generated content at work?

This is ‘workslop’: AI-written content that looks good - but which is, in fact, so low in quality that it creates more work for the person on the receiving end. 

40% of US workers say they have been sent #workslop, in a survey by BetterUp and Stanford Social Media Lab. And as bringing a piece of workslop up to scratch can take around two hours, it’s costing businesses in lost productivity. 

Here, Alexi Robichaux, CEO of BetterUp, explains the problem, alongside some possible solutions.

Alexi Robichaux was a guest on #MeetTheLeader, a World Economic Forum video podcast. Watch the full episode: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zTAbIqqAf4Y

result.title: AI and Jobs Series: What one company stopped doing - an HR exec weighs in
result.description:
As AI grows more powerful and takes on more rote work, what should humans stop doing? Fertility benefits company Progyny took on this question as a company to re-evaluate routines and norms and how AI might help work evolve. Chief Human Resources Officer Cassandra Pratt shares how her team is using AI to reduce rote work, rethink job design, improve meeting culture and give people more time for the human side of work that machines cannot do: building trust, creativity and stronger relationships. The first in a three-part AI and Jobs series.

Key takeaways:

-The importance of clear goals and prep during AI implementation
-How the “Start, Stop, Continue” framework from author Barry O’Reilly can reduce burnout and sharpen execution
-How to turn teams into superfans of your company and business to strengthen engagement
-What fluid job design will look like in the years ahead - and how to help teams navigate it

About this episode:
Progyny: https://progyny.com/

Book: Unlearn: Let Go of Past Success to Achieve Extraordinary Results, Barry O’Reilly
Report: 2026 Chief People Officer Outlook, World Economic Forum:  https://www.weforum.org/publications/chief-people-officers-outlook-may-2026/
